newsitem.title: USA: N. Calif. voters approve school bonds, taxes.
newsitem.headline: N. Calif. voters approve school bonds, taxes.

text.p: Voters across northern California approved bonds to fix schools and tax measures to maintain fire protection services, according to election officials and published reports on Wednesday.

Pleasanton voters approved Measure B, a $70 million bond measure to fund school improvements, by a substantial margin, the San Francisco Chronicle reported. In San Leandro, voters approved Measure A, a $54 million school bond.
In Piedmont, voters passed two taxes. Measure C will allows the school district to levy a tax designed to generate nearly $2 million per year over the next four years.
Piedmont residents also passed Measure D, a four-year tax that will raise about $500,000 per year for school improvements, election officials said.
Burlingame voters approved measures to modernize its schools and reopen an 89-year-old facility. The measures included two parcel taxes and a $6 million bond measure.

In Marin and Sonoma counties, all of the property tax measures to maintain fire protection services and improve education won the needed two-thirds majority vote, the San Francisco Chronicle reported.

Many of Tuesday's measures were on the ballot because of Proposition 218, a statewide initiative approved last November. The proposition requires voter approval of an array of taxes, assessments and fees levied by local governments.
